_meta.vector_method: SHA-256-free. ELEM_ uses Z-based Gray code (real atomic number). All other entries use MOG-presence bits (bit i = 1 if MOG category i has data). Text-only math falls back to keyword-based MOG mapping (directive §4.2). SHA-256 is used ONLY as the top-level `fingerprint` tag for fast recall.
_meta.notes: Vectors re-derived via KBArchitect.generate_vector(math, ubp_id) with the v3.0 SHA-256-free patch. Duplicates merged with `aliases` array. `meta` carries entry-specific extras (chromatic data for elements, pos/role for words).

[Math: Avogadro Constant], [The Avogadro constant (NA) is a fundamental physical constant equal to exactly 6.02214076e23 per mole. It is the number of constituent particles (atoms, molecules, ions) in one mole of a substance. NA defines the mole via SI units and connects macroscopic and atomic scales. It is named after Amedeo Avogadro.]

[Math: Boltzmann Constant], [The Boltzmann constant (kB) is a fundamental physical constant equal to exactly 1.380649e-23 joules per kelvin. It relates the average kinetic energy of particles to temperature: E = (3/2) kB T. The Boltzmann constant defines the kelvin via SI units and appears in statistical mechanics, thermodynamics, and the ideal gas law.]

[Math: Electron Mass], [The electron mass (me) is a fundamental physical constant equal to 9.1093837015e-31 kilograms or 0.51099895 MeV/c^2. It is the rest mass of the electron. The proton-to-electron mass ratio is 1836.15. The electron mass sets the scale of atomic physics and chemistry. It appears in the Bohr model, Schrodinger equation, and QED.]

[Math: Elementary Charge], [The elementary charge (e) is the electric charge carried by a single proton, equal to exactly 1.602176634e-19 coulombs. It is the fundamental unit of electric charge. The electron carries charge -e. The elementary charge defines the ampere via SI units and appears in all electromagnetic phenomena involving charged particles.]

[Math: Fine Structure Constant], [The fine structure constant (alpha) is a dimensionless fundamental constant approximately equal to 1/137.036. It characterises the strength of the electromagnetic interaction. Alpha = e^2 / (4 pi epsilon_0 hbar c). Its value determines the scale of atomic structure and the splitting of spectral lines. It is one of the most precisely measured constants.]

[Math: Gravitational Constant], [The gravitational constant (G) is a fundamental physical constant equal to 6.67430e-11 N m^2 kg^-2. It appears in Newton's law of gravitation: F = G m1 m2 / r^2. G also appears in Einstein's field equations of general relativity. It is the least precisely measured fundamental constant.]
